known_information: The reporter says a local shortcut remap works and Copilot launches instead when using Remote Desktop over a VPN.
The report does not say whether PowerToys runs locally, remotely or both, or how the RDP Windows-key routing option is configured.
The only reply advertises a third-party remapper; it is not evidence that a PowerToys fix shipped or that a VPN causes the routing failure.
issue_context.analysis: First distinguish local chord interception from remote delivery and remote-host interpretation. A local user-mode remap is not a permanent physical-key rewrite across every session. Do not install an advertised tool or attribute the problem to VPN encryption without evidence.
issue_context.summary: Copilot-to-rightCtrl works locally but not over RDP; input routing and the Keyboard Manager execution side are still unspecified.
initial_investigation: Read complete issue, discussion and timeline; separated third-party promotion from evidence. Compared the reported chord-to-key operation with the per-process/session nature of Keyboard Manager input handling.
No remote session, VPN configuration, remapper installation or keyboard input was changed.

information_gaps.why_needed: These identify which input boundary loses or bypasses the intended remap.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: State where Keyboard Manager is running, the Remote Desktop Local Resources keyboard option and whether local or remote Copilot opens; no hostnames, VPN details or full settings export are needed.
information_gaps.information: Local/remote PowerToys placement, RDP keyboard-routing option and endpoint opening Copilot

inferences: Windows-key routing can change where a Copilot chord is handled; the current report does not establish the order for this setup.

proposed_fixes.root_cause: Unverified hypothesis: the RDP client forwards or consumes the original Windows/Shift/F23 chord before the intended local or remote remap path sees it.

confidence.rationale: Local-versus-remote contrast is clear, but session placement and client routing that determine interception are missing.

plan: Record the local/remote PowerToys placement and RDP Windows-key routing setting.
Compare local desktop, windowed RDP and full-screen RDP with the same remap, observing which endpoint opens Copilot.
Correct only the demonstrated supported routing path or document its limitation; do not assume a VPN or permanent firmware remap.
proposed_fixes.title: Isolate Copilot remapping across the RDP input boundary
verification: The chosen supported configuration yields rightCtrl behavior on the intended endpoint.
Copilot does not open on either unintended endpoint during that sequence.
Ordinary Ctrl/Windows shortcuts and remaps outside RDP retain their behavior.

actions.label: Identify local versus remote key routing

comment.body: Since the remap works on the local desktop, the next distinction is where the Copilot chord is handled during RDP. Please state whether Keyboard Manager runs on the local PC, remote PC or both; which Remote Desktop → Local Resources → Keyboard option is selected; and whether Copilot opens on the local or remote computer. No VPN details, hostnames or full settings export are needed. The third-party tool linked above is not a PowerToys fix, and we should not assume the VPN itself causes this input-routing difference.

fix_assessment.rationale: A targeted session-routing investigation is applicable, but there is not enough configuration evidence to choose a code change.

judgment.rationale: First distinguish local chord interception from remote delivery and remote-host interpretation. A local user-mode remap is not a permanent physical-key rewrite across every session. Do not install an advertised tool or attribute the problem to VPN encryption without evidence.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask only where Keyboard Manager runs, the RDP keyboard-routing setting and which computer opens Copilot.
evidence: The reporter says a local shortcut remap works and Copilot launches instead when using Remote Desktop over a VPN.
The report does not say whether PowerToys runs locally, remotely or both, or how the RDP Windows-key routing option is configured.
The only reply advertises a third-party remapper; it is not evidence that a PowerToys fix shipped or that a VPN causes the routing failure.
